title: The symmetric algebra
source: Stacks, Algebra §10.13; D05 K05.15.symmetric is the field case.
proof_check: The commutators generate a homogeneous ideal starting in degree two.

title: Universal symmetric multilinear maps
source: Stacks, Algebra Lemma 10.13.3; Conrad, Bases of Symmetric and Exterior Powers, definition and multilinear description.
proof_check: Adjacent transpositions give the degree-wise relations. Degree zero evaluates at the unit.

title: The free commutative algebra property
source: Stacks, Algebra §10.13, symmetric-algebra construction; free algebra property deduced here.
proof_check: The degree-wise maps respect multiplication because they do so on the pure classes.

title: The monomial basis of a finite free module
source: Conrad, Bases of Symmetric and Exterior Powers, Theorem 1.2 and proof; Stacks, Algebra Lemma 10.13.1.
proof_check: Universal properties give the graded polynomial identification, including degree zero and the empty basis.

title: Arbitrary base change
source: Stacks, Sheaves of Modules Lemma 17.21.3, specialized to one-point ringed spaces; Algebra Lemma 10.14.3. RK-04 gives the related exterior comparison.
proof_check: The inverse maps and all compatibility statements follow on degree-one generators and scalars. No flatness premise.

title: A torsion module and nonflat base change
source: Direct calculation in this supplement; Stacks, Algebra §10.14, base change of algebra presentations.
proof_check: The relation 2X gives one cyclic torsion module in each positive degree. Reduction modulo 2 is nonflat.

title: The quotient in characteristic two
source: Direct calculation in this supplement; D05 K05.15.normalization gives the averaging background.
proof_check: Over F2 the invariant mixed-tensor sum maps to zero, while the mixed monomial survives.

title: Splitting a hyperbolic plane
proof_check: The second hyperbolic vector is adjusted using B(e,f0)=1/2 and the convention q_H(x,y)=xy.

title: Moving vectors of the same nonzero value
source: Elman–Karpenko–Merkurjev, Ch. II, Example 7.2 (printed p. 40), Eq. (8.1) and Lemma 8.2 (printed p. 47).
proof_check: The u−v reflection suffices when anisotropic; otherwise q(u+v)=4q(u) and two reflections suffice.

title: Witt cancellation
source: Elman–Karpenko–Merkurjev, Ch. II, Theorem 8.4 (printed p. 48); Lam, Ch. I, Section 4.
proof_check: Cancel a nondegenerate line by moving its image, then apply diagonalization to cancel the remaining lines.

title: Witt decomposition and uniqueness
source: Elman–Karpenko–Merkurjev, Ch. II, Theorem 8.5 (printed pp. 48–49); Lam, Ch. I, Section 4.
proof_check: Each splitting lowers dimension by two. Cancellation and anisotropy give the unique hyperbolic count and anisotropic isometry type.

title: Totally isotropic subspaces and the Witt index
source: Elman–Karpenko–Merkurjev, Ch. II, Lemma 8.10, Proposition 8.11, and Corollary 8.12 (printed p. 50).
proof_check: A totally isotropic subspace supplies the first isotropic lines of an orthogonal hyperbolic sum, including the zero-dimensional case.

title: A Witt index that increases after extending scalars
source: Direct calculation in this supplement, using the Witt decomposition.
proof_check: The binary plane has no nonzero isotropic vector over Q and splits explicitly over Q(sqrt(2)).
